summary: The paper develops quantum amplitude-estimation-based algorithms for EVaR and RVaR, and evaluates them alongside VaR and CVaR on two case studies: a 2-asset credit-risk portfolio and calibrated insurance-claim distributions (lognormal and gamma). Reported experiments use 2 qubits for the latent normal factor in the credit-risk model, 3-5 qubits for distribution loading in the insurance study, and m = 3, 4, 5 ancilla qubits for canonical QAE; the main finding is that EVaR/VaR are relatively robust on noisy simulators, while CVaR/RVaR are much more noise-sensitive.

experiments.description: Canonical quantum amplitude estimation, maximum-likelihood QAE, and iterative QAE used to estimate Value-at-Risk, Conditional Value-at-Risk, Expectile Value-at-Risk, and Range Value-at-Risk for a two-asset credit-risk portfolio under varying ancilla counts and on noiseless/noisy simulators.

algorithm.variant: canonical QAE, MLQAE, and IQAE applied to risk-measure estimation
algorithm.convergence_criteria: For expectiles, classical bisection stops when |y| < ϵ or interval half-width < δ; QAE variants use target precision/confidence or fixed ancilla count as reported

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Distribution of the loss random variable L is loaded into an n-qubit register; comparator circuits and controlled Ry rotations encode the payoff/risk-measure function for amplitude estimation
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate expectations/conditional expectations needed for VaR, CVaR, EVaR, and RVaR via amplitude estimation; for EVaR, solve h_X,α(x)=x by bisection where h_X,α(x)=E[max{(1+β)X−βx,X}]
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Comparator circuits define tail events; conditional expectation for RVaR uses probability p of the interval between VaR thresholds
problem_formulation.num_ancilla_qubits: m ancilla qubits for canonical QAE; additional ancillas used inside comparator circuits and distribution loading

problem_instance.description: Two-asset credit-risk portfolio with correlated defaults driven by a latent normal factor

dataset_specification.latent_factor: standard normal Z discretized on [-2,2] with 2 qubits
dataset_specification.loss_model: L = L1 + L2, where Lk = λk Xk

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Standard normal distribution restricted to [-2,2]; default probabilities approximated by first-order expansion of 2 arcsin(sqrt(p_k(z))) around z=0; loss distribution loaded via quantum circuit
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Average result over 1000 executions for varying ancilla qubits; comparison on noiseless and noisy simulators; error relative to exact value

implementation_details.transpilation_target: IBM Brisbane noise model / Qiskit backend
implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical bisection search for EVaR; classical postprocessing for risk-measure reconstruction
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Discretization of continuous distributions; calibration of default probabilities via first-order approximation; construction of comparator thresholds from VaR estimates
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Bisection search for expectiles; reconstruction of RVaR from estimated probability p and conditional expectation

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: For expectiles, bisection converges; for QAE variants, estimates approach exact values as ancilla count increases

speedup_claims.conditions: via quantum amplitude estimation; assumes suitable quantum implementation
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the quadratic reduction in computation time as a promise of amplitude estimation, but does not provide a measured wall-clock speedup.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Quadratic speedup from amplitude estimation relative to Monte Carlo is claimed in the introduction; no paper-specific asymptotic bound beyond QAE is given
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Monte Carlo-based estimation is the classical baseline; no explicit asymptotic bound stated

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not reported; only small credit-risk toy instance with 2 assets and 2 qubits for latent factor loading
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Amplitude estimation with m ancilla qubits (m = 3, 4, 5 in the study) plus comparator ancillas and distribution-loading qubits; no end-to-end resource estimate for practical advantage

No classical runtime comparison on the same problem size

num_qubits combines explicitly reported 2-qubit latent normal register, 2 qubits for Bernoulli variables, 2 qubits for losses, and m ancilla qubits for canonical QAE; exact total depends on the chosen QAE variant and comparator ancillas.

problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate VaR/CVaR/EVaR/RVaR from discretized lognormal and gamma distributions; EVaR via root search on h_X,α(x)=E[max{(1+β)X−βx,X}]
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Comparator circuits for VaR thresholds; RVaR uses two comparators and conditional expectation with estimated interval probability p
problem_formulation.num_ancilla_qubits: m ancilla qubits for canonical QAE; additional ancillas in comparator circuits

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Fit lognormal and gamma distributions to the cleaned dataset; discretize the support into 2^n points; use the distribution of -Y for risk-measure calculations
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compare estimation error versus number of qubits and versus number of shots; noisy-simulator experiments emulate a real device; results reported for both lognormal and gamma cases

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Bisection search for expectiles; reconstruct RVaR from estimated interval probability and conditional expectation
